newsitem.title: USA: Cone Mills to take $0.20/shr charge in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Cone Mills to take $0.20/shr charge in Q4.

text.p: Cone Mills Corp said on Tuesday that it has taken additional steps in the company's program to refocus on its core businesses and facilities and will take a charge in the fourth quarter of $5 million, or $0.20 a share.

The steps include the sale of Greeff Fabrics, part of the Cone Decorative Fabrics group, the sale of the synthetic fabric business, a part of the Cone Sportswear division, the expected sale of the assets of Cornwallis Development Co, Cone's real estate subsidiary and the planned closing of the Granite Finishing Plant in Haw River, North Carolina.
The company said it expects to receive proceeds of about $24 million on the sale of Greeff, Cornwallis, and the synthetic fabric business.
Sales of these three units were about $30 million in 1996.

"For some time, Cone's management has been working to refocus the company's operations on its core businesses: the manufacture and marketing of high quality denim, sportswear, and home furnishings fabrics as well as commission finishing services," J. Patrick Danahy, Cone's president and chief executive officer, said in a press release.
Last year, the company sold its polyurethane foam division, Olympic Products.

According to Cone, the sale of Greeff, which is a distributor of higher fashion fabrics, to F. Schumacher & Co is part of a recent repositioning of Cone Decorative Fabrics to return as a major supplier to broader home furnishings industry segments.
Cone Decorative will offer a wide line of printed, jacquard, yarn-dyed and solid products to this industry, the company said.
Cone said it has sold its synthetic fabric business to Majestic Mills in a transaction that includes Cone's finished inventory of synthetic fabric, forward commitments and order book.
The company said that with this sale, Cone Sportswear will be better able to focus on its core areas of shirtings, prints, bottom-weight and specialty fabrics.
Cone said it has received several bids for its Cornwallis Development real estate subsidiary and has begun negotiations.
If successful, the company should consummate the transaction in the first part of 1997, it said.
With the Granite Finishing Plant's closing, the plant's dyeing and finishing production will be moved to Cone's Carlisle Plant in Carlisle, South Carolina.
The production phaseout at Granite will begin in mid-April and will continue until the end of July 1997.
At the conclusion of the phaseout, a small warehouse and fabric-cutting operation will remain at Granite until the end of 1997, at which time operations will be discontinued.
